transcript:
<meeting header>
Date: 2026-04-09
Start: 2026-04-09 15:30 PDT
Duration: 53 minutes (recording ended at 16:23)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Nebula Head of AI), Liam O'Neill (Nebula Eng Mgr), Priya Rao (Nebula Security/Compliance)
Meeting ID: ff-2026-04-09-nebula-6821

Summary:
Short kickoff to align on pilot success criteria, define the 'precision assurance' quality baseline (golden prompts + hallucination checks), and agree on benchmark sizing and timeline. Customer stressed PII handling and on-prem routing for some workloads.

Topics Covered:
- Acceptance criteria (latency, accuracy, acceptable hallucination rates)
- Defining golden prompts / goldset + regression playlist
- Workload sizing: avg tokens, peak QPS, concurrency
- Benchmarks: throughput/latency measurement plan, scoring approach
- Security requirements: KMS, audit logs, VPC connectivity
- Timeline & next steps

Action items (recap at end included): see metadata

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya: Maya here, hi. Sorry I'm on mobile, bit of background noise.
[00:10] Liam: Liam O'Neill, eng manager, good to see you.
[00:12] Priya: Priya Rao from security, I'll listen for compliance items.
[00:16] Samir: Samir Patel, I'll drive the benchmark side and technical scoping.

[02:05] Alex: High level — Nebula's goal is to run a four week pilot to validate precision on named-entity extraction and response summarization flows, plus prove latency at our production scale, right?
[02:18] Maya: Yes, precisely. For us "precision" means low hallucination for entity values and consistent JSON-ish output for downstream parsers. If we get inconsistent format it breaks our pipelines.
[02:34] Liam: And also we want to confirm cost per call at QPS peaks; we don't want surprising token bills.

[05:00] Samir: Ok, so acceptance criteria we usually split into two buckets: quality and performance. For quality we recommend a golden set of ~500 prompts covering edge cases, plus a regression playlist of a further ~2k queries for statistical confidence. For perf we need to measure p50/p95/p99 latency at baseline and under burst.
[05:27] Maya: 500 seems fair but can we start smaller if we need to? We have 300 curated cases now.
[05:33] Alex: Absolutely, start with 300 golden prompts and expand; we'll help with curation guidelines. The important part is they reflect your real failure modes.

[08:10] Priya: On security — we need to know where data stays, encryption in transit and at rest, and KMS integration. We prefer customer-managed keys. Any reason that would be a blocker for Redwood Dedicated or Private?
[08:28] Samir: No blocker, we support KMS integrations and our Private deployment can run inside a VPC with KMS/HSM — sometimes the transcripting engines call it the "Redwood private plane" in notes, but it's basically a customer-controlled control plane.
[08:48] Priya: (laughs) yeah sometimes transcriptions show the funny names. We'll need audit log samples and a short threat model for the pilot.

[12:20] Liam: For workload sizing: current prod baseline is 60 qps sustained during business hours, 180 qps peak bursts for short windows. Typical request is 120 tokens in prompt and 200 tokens generated on average.
[12:36] Samir: That's helpful — for benchmarking we'll plan runs at 60 qps sustained, 180 qps mimic burst, and a concurrency test to exercise KV cache and batching. Do you have any long context sessions ( > 1k tokens )?
[12:53] Maya: Rare, maybe 5% of sessions exceed 1k tokens; mostly short dialogs.

[15:05] Alex: On the golden prompts and scoring: we propose a three-part scoring for each golden case — correctness (binary or graded), hallucination flag (did it invent extra entities), and format adherence (JSON schema match). We can combine into a weighted score; customer decides weights.
[15:28] Maya: We care about hallucination first then strict format. So maybe weight hallucination 50%, format 30%, correctness 20%.
[15:39] Samir: Noted. We'll include that as a default scoring and show how to tweak it in the eval dashboard.

[18:00] Liam: How do you measure hallucination? Can you give examples?
[18:08] Samir: Sure — one golden prompt: "Extract organization and role from text." If model outputs an organization not present in the text, that's a hallucination. We flag extra entities or fabricated facts. We can run fuzzy matching to account for OCR noise but strict on introducing new facts.
[18:32] Maya: For our domain we also want semantic hallucination checks — e.g., if model assigns wrong taxonomy labels but with high confidence that's problematic.

[21:12] Alex: Regarding regression tests — want to run daily smoke checks and a weekly full regression pass. The regression playlist will exercise known failure modes plus random sampling from production logs (redacted) to ensure we don't regress on coverage.
[21:35] Priya: We won't be able to share raw logs with PII; we'll provide redacted versions and a synthetic set that mimics patterns.
[21:44] Samir: That's good — synthetic plus redacted is standard.

[24:00] Maya: On benchmarks, we need a runbook. What's the typical approach?
[24:10] Samir: We'll spin up a test harness that hits the same model and routing you'd use in pilot. Tests we propose: cold start latency, steady state throughput with concurrency, prefix-caching efficacy, token-level cost calculation. We'll provide the harness repo and scripts; you run it in your VPC or we can run it on Redwood Dedicated with controlled data.
[24:41] Liam: If we run it in our VPC, what network requirements are there?
[24:47] Samir: Just outbound to our control plane and a few endpoints for health checks; we'll send a network matrix. For Private/on-prem we can do fully closed runs.

[28:03] Maya: Timeline check — we proposed a four week pilot. What's Redwood's recommended cadence?
[28:12] Alex: Week 0: kickoff + gather goldset and dataset samples. Week 1: baseline runs and initial quality gating. Week 2: targeted tuning (prompting / quantization tweaks) and regression. Week 3: final acceptance tests and runbook handoff. We usually allow a week buffer for security approvals.
[28:37] Maya: That fits. We need executive signoff by May 10th to hit our product release dates.

[31:05] Priya: On compliance deliverables — can you share SOC2 cert, pen test summary, and data flows? Also need contract language for data retention.
[31:18] Alex: Yes, we'll send SOC2 report and sample contract clauses. We can also include an NDA addendum for the pilot.

[33:40] Liam: Performance benchmarks — how do we score cost tradeoffs? We sometimes accept small latency increases for 30% cost savings.
[33:50] Samir: We'll include a cost-performance matrix in the report: model variant (quantized vs fp16), p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens. We'll recommend routes based on your SLO. Also, we'll show automatic fallback policies: if latency spikes, route to cheaper variant with similar output distribution.

[36:55] Maya: Regarding golden prompts — do you provide templates? We can craft but want your guidance.
[37:04] Samir: Yes, Samir will send a golden prompt template and a short rubric for tagging edge cases (ambiguous entities, nested entities, inconsistent format). We'll also provide a small set of Redwood-curated examples for the domain to seed the goldset.
[37:24] Alex: We'll also propose a small human labeling plan — 3 raters per item for the golden set to get agreement scores.

[40:50] Priya: Audit logs — what granularity do you keep? We need token-level usage per request and identity mapping.
[40:58] Samir: We capture request/response metadata, timestamps, model variant, and cost estimate. We don't store raw prompt text unless configured; for pilot we'll follow your redaction preferences.

[44:15] Maya: One question on regression thresholds — what's an acceptable hallucination rate change to fail the gate?
[44:23] Alex: Typical baseline: <1% hallucination on golden set. For pilot we can set a target of <2% and alert if regression >0.5% relative to baseline. But we should align on the real numbers after the first run.
[44:40] Maya: Sounds reasonable.

[47:10] Liam: Any competitor pitfalls we should know? We tried another vendor and their batching caused inconsistent outputs under concurrency.
[47:19] Samir: We design continuous batching and KV cache carefully to avoid cross-request leakage; we'll include isolation tests in the perf suite.

[49:30] Alex: Ok recap and next steps: We'll send SOW and security pack by Monday (4/12). Samir sends benchmark plan and golden prompt template by Wed (4/14). Maya to provide redacted dataset and PII rules by Tue (4/13). We'll schedule the benchmark execution window for week of 4/19.
[49:57] Maya: Confirmed.
[50:02] Priya: I'll review SOC2 and send any clarifying questions.
[50:08] Liam: I'll coordinate infra access for the week of 4/19.

[52:00] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links. End call.

[52:10] (recording stops)
